static_findings.observation: Normalization restricts where subjects to directly declared ordinary type binders. It reuses Index::declaration before aliases and feeds nominal obligations back to existing generic checking; no new impl or field/callable/Copy permission is introduced.
The module visitor resolves each where subject and bound with the same local type-binder set used for inline bounds. Index declaration and impl matching retain the complete canonical identity.

Only a dollar-module prefix followed by nonempty decimal digits and an underscore is stripped for the reserved-name exclusion; full names remain declaration/impl keys. Similar ordinary names are not split arbitrarily.
trait_bounds::plain uses grouped traversal for nominal bounds. Direct built-in Copy retains the existing 229 syntax boundary, and projected/compound subjects remain excluded.

The module clone is prepaid. The lazy new Index is preceded by item/name/type traversal; nominal bounds and deduplication scans spend the same request budget. Actual boundary measurements remain pending.
Copy repetitions are collapsed. Nominal repetitions remain visible to existing duplicate-bound checks, including inline plus where occurrences.

The three module example sources have new explicit identities and matching recorded byte/SHA256/Git hashes. They exercise real aliased module identity and generic shared-parameter forwarding; no historical thresholds are adopted.
